We need to determine number of C=O groups in the compound. We have no SMILES given. We need to get IR spectra maybe to see carbonyl stretch. But we could also get carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons. However we need the compound identity. Possibly the system has a sample at hand (some unknown). We need to measure IR to detect C=O. Use ir_spectra tool. That will give IR peaks, we can count carbonyl stretches (~1700 cm-1). Could be ambiguous. Maybe better to get carbon NMR: carbonyl carbons appear around 190-220 ppm. Count peaks in that region.

We need to minimize cost. IR is cheaper? Not sure. Both are single calls. Use IR first. If IR shows carbonyl peaks, count them. Let's call ir_spectra.
